question: Name a unit designed for wet and dry bulb thermometers to protect temperature sensors from being affected by direct or reflected sunlight.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Stevenson screen**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **A Stevenson screen **serves as a protective shelter for meteorological instruments, such as **wet and dry bulb thermometers,** safeguarding them from direct sunlight and precipitation while facilitating free airflow.
 
• These screens are typically constructed from wood and painted white to reflect solar radiation effectively.
 
• Featuring louvered sides, Stevenson screens enable unrestricted air circulation around the thermometers, ensuring accurate temperature measurements.
 
• Moreover, they are strategically positioned 1.25 meters above the ground to minimize the influence of strong temperature gradients present at ground level.
 
• Thomas Stevenson, a notable Scottish civil engineer, credited with the design of the Stevenson screen in 1864. He is also recognized as the father of the renowned writer Robert Louis Stevenson.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Thomas Stevenson **was a pioneering Scottish civil engineer, renowned for his contributions to lighthouse design and meteorology. He designed over thirty lighthouses in and around Scotland, as well as the Stevenson screen used in meteorology.
 
• His innovative designs revolutionized lighthouse construction and set a new standard in the field.
 
• Stevenson held prestigious positions throughout his career, including serving as president of the Royal Scottish Society of Arts from 1859 to 1860 and as president of the Royal Society of Edinburgh from 1884 to 1886.
 
• Additionally, he played a key role as a co-founder of the Scottish Meteorological Society.
